title: FLY_TO_DESTINATION flies a straight line to a destination dead ahead, slows down and posts shipAchievedDesiredRange once inside desiredRange
derivation: A Viper-like ship at the origin facing +z at rest, destination (0, 0, 3000) dead ahead, desired_range 500, desired_speed 320, all set through assign. behaviour_fly_to_destination (ShipEntity.m:5049-5134) tracks the destination with trackDestination (dead ahead: d_forward = 1 is above max_cos, so the sticks stay 0 and the function returns 1.0, 9517 and 9587-9588), and then applyThrust ramps the speed at 5 * thrust per second (4/3 per tick). Early ticks are closed forms: flightSpeed = 4k/3 and position z = k(k+1)/180 (the eta rule cannot fire while eta is far above slowdownTime). From the point where eta < slowdownTime and flightSpeed > maxFlightSpeed * minTurnSpeedFactor (5095), desired_speed is halved on every tick the rule holds (5096), so the speed steps down 320 -> 160 -> 80: those values and the arrival come from the reference replay (the same transliteration, in Oolite's float32 emulation), with tolerances from the measured float32-versus-float64 difference. The ship posts shipAchievedDesiredRange once, on the tick the centre distance first falls below desired_range (5053-5057), and in that same update switches to IDLE with desired_speed 0 and frustration 0 (5061-5064): it decelerates to rest from then on, because IDLE keeps applying thrust (ShipEntity.m:2634-2637). Arrival is at tick 1885: the update reads the position of tick 1884, 0.33 m inside desired_range, one closing step (0.67 m at 80 m/s) after a position 0.33 m outside it; the float32-versus-float64 distance difference there is 4e-4 m, so both widths cross on the same tick.

title: FLY_TO_DESTINATION with the destination dead behind pitches up with the d_up hack, turns around and flies to the destination
derivation: The destination (0, 0, -2500) is exactly behind a ship at rest facing +z. trackDestination finds d_forward = -1, which is <= -max_cos, so the hack at ShipEntity.m:9520-9523 replaces d_up by 2 * min_d = 0.008 and the pitch branch runs: d_right is 0, so no roll; factor = int(sqrt(0.008 / 0.004)) = int(1.414) = 1 and stick_pitch = -max_flight_pitch * reverse * 0.125 * factor = -1.8 * 0.125 = -0.225 at tick 1 (closed form), ramping at 1/30 per tick. As the nose rises d_up grows and the factor reaches 8 (stick -1.8) until the nose is within the dead band max_cos = sqrt(1 - 0.9025 * desired_range^2 / range^2) (9486-9490); the later values are replayed by the reference (float32 emulation) with tolerances from the float32-versus-float64 difference. The u-turn costs distance (the ship accelerates while turning), and the arrival at tick 1934 switches to IDLE (5053-5064). The heading error at the end of the approach is not zero: the ship stops steering once the destination sphere is inside the dead band (the 95 % rule of trackDestination), so it arrives at an angle.

title: a destination exactly abeam leaves both d_up thresholds unmet, so trackDestination falls back to the 0.01 pitch stick
derivation: The destination (5000, 0, 0) is exactly to the right of a ship at rest facing +z: d_right = 1, d_up = 0, d_forward = 0. d_forward < max_cos, so the correction block runs, but |d_up| is not above min_d = 0.004, so neither roll branch fires (ShipEntity.m:9525 and 9537), stick_roll stays 0, the pitch branch computes factor 0 and leaves stick_pitch at 0, and the final fallback gives stick_pitch = 0.01 (9561-9565) every tick. flightPitch snaps onto 0.01 at tick 1 and stays there, and the ship pitches slowly nose-down while it accelerates (the stall of an abeam target is Oolite's own behaviour; the roll only starts once d_up leaves the +-0.004 band, after the horizon). The 0.01 values are closed forms; the heading errors and the range come from the reference replay with tolerances from the float32-versus-float64 difference.

title: a destination above and to the right makes trackDestination roll first (negative stick_roll) and skip the pitch branch
derivation: The destination (5000, 5000, 0) is at 45 degrees up and to the right of a ship at rest facing +z: d_right = d_up = 0.7071, d_forward = 0. In the d_up > min_d block, factor = int(sqrt(0.7071 / 0.004)) = 13, capped at 8, and d_right > min_d gives stick_roll = -max_flight_roll * reversePlayer * 0.125 * 8 = -2.8 (ShipEntity.m:9525-9531): a NEGATIVE roll to bring the up vector toward the target on the right, the sense the attitude-step fixtures show. The overshoot limiter does not bind (|d_right| = 0.7071 is far above 2.8 / 120). Because stick_roll is not 0 the pitch branch (9549) is skipped, and the fallback sets stick_pitch = 0.01 (9561-9565). The roll rate ramps at 1/60 per tick, so flightRoll = -k/60 while the stick stays saturated (checked up to tick 60, where the ship has rolled 0.25 rad). Later headings come from the reference replay with tolerances from the float32-versus-float64 difference.

title: FLY_RANGE_FROM_DESTINATION hands over to FLY_TO_DESTINATION when the destination is at or beyond desiredRange
derivation: assign perform FLY_RANGE_FROM_DESTINATION with the destination (0, 0, 3000), desired_range 1000 and desired_speed 160 at rest. performFlyToRangeFromDestination sets the behaviour and frustration 0 (ShipEntityAI.m:394-398), so tick 0 shows FLY_RANGE_FROM_DESTINATION. The first update runs behaviour_fly_range_from_destination (ShipEntity.m:4903-4918): the distance 3000 is not below desired_range 1000, so behaviour = FLY_TO_DESTINATION, desired_speed is untouched, and frustration = 0. That function neither tracks nor calls applySticks, so no stick changes this tick; processBehaviour then applies the attitude and thrust (2634-2637), so the ship already accelerates by 4/3. The eta rule cannot cut the speed (eta about 24 s against slowdownTime 5 s), so flightSpeed = min(160, 4k/3). All values are closed forms.

title: FLY_RANGE_FROM_DESTINATION hands over to FLY_FROM_DESTINATION inside desiredRange and raises desiredSpeed to maxFlightSpeed
derivation: assign perform FLY_RANGE_FROM_DESTINATION with the destination (0, 0, 600) dead ahead, desired_range 2000 and desired_speed 100. At the first update distance 600 < desired_range 2000, so behaviour = FLY_FROM_DESTINATION and desired_speed, below max_flight_speed 320, is raised to 320 (ShipEntity.m:4906-4910). No tracking runs that tick, so the sticks and rates stay 0, and applyThrust ramps toward 320 (4/3 per tick). From tick 2 behaviour_fly_from_destination runs trackDestination with retreat = YES: the destination dead ahead has d_forward = 1 >= max_cos, which with retreat triggers the d_up hack (9520), and the pitch branch gives stick_pitch = -max_flight_pitch * (-1) * 0.125 * 1 = +0.225, so flightPitch = 1/30 at tick 2 (closed forms). The ship is not yet beyond desired_range 2000 within the horizon, so no event. Heading and range at later ticks come from the reference replay.

title: FLY_FROM_DESTINATION flies away until the centre distance exceeds desiredRange, posts shipAchievedDesiredRange once and switches to IDLE with desiredSpeed 0
derivation: A ship at rest facing +z with the destination (0, 0, -600) behind it, desired_range 1500 and desired_speed 100 in FLY_FROM_DESTINATION. Each update runs behaviour_fly_from_destination (ShipEntity.m:5136-5153): trackDestination with retreat = YES (the sense is 'turn away'), here with d_forward = -1, takes the d_up hack and sets stick_pitch = +0.225 on tick 1 (closed form); the retreat pattern then alternates its pitch while it flies away at 100 m/s (a feature of the retreat hack; replayed by the reference). When the centre distance first exceeds desired_range, the function posts shipAchievedDesiredRange, sets behaviour IDLE, frustration 0 and desired_speed 0 (5139-5147) and still runs trackDestination in the same update, so this tick's sticks are the retreat sticks; the next update (IDLE) zeroes them. The speed then falls at 4/3 per tick (100 - 4/3 on the event tick, 100 - 61 * 4/3 sixty ticks later, 0 at 76 ticks). The event tick is 1124 (the ship recedes by 0.83 m per tick at 100 m/s, and the position the update reads is 0.5 m beyond desired_range, against a float32-versus-float64 difference of 1e-4 m). The event posts once because the behaviour is no longer FLY_FROM_DESTINATION afterwards.

title: a FLY_TO_DESTINATION ship that cannot improve its distance posts shipAIFrustrated once frustration exceeds 15 s, and again every tick while it stays above
derivation: A ship at rest with desired_speed 0, 10000 m from its destination (0, 0, 10000) dead ahead, desired_range 100. The distance never changes, so `distance < last_distance` is false on every tick (10000 is exactly representable in float32, so the test is the same in both widths) and each tick does frustration += delta_t (ShipEntity.m:5122-5123). frustration is GLfloat, so by contract item 8 the sum is accumulated with Math.fround at every step: it first exceeds 15.0 at tick 1801 (the same sum in float64 also crosses at 1801; the expected values are the fround accumulation, computed by the helper loop, not seconds * 120). At that tick `frustration > 15.0` holds, the ship posts shipAIFrustrated (noteFrustration, 5126) and subtracts slowdownTime * 5.0 (5127). slowdownTime = flightSpeed / thrust = 0 for a ship at rest, so nothing is subtracted, frustration stays above 15 and the event repeats on every later tick: it is listed once per tick (contract item 2), which is why the horizon ends at tick 1803. The first clause (frustration > slowdownTime * 10.0 && slowdownTime > 0) cannot fire for a ship at rest.
